# German Shepherd research receipt

Research date: 2026-09-25. The original model is retained here as a reproducible source for the adapted Khloé model. The unmodified distribution license is retained as LICENSE.original.txt. This source is CC0 according to the author’s specific pack page and original announcement; the mirror’s mismatched boilerplate pack heading is documented below.

## Preferred author and asset

- Author: **Quaternius**.
- Pack: **Zombie Apocalypse Kit**, March 2024.
- Official pack and license declaration: https://quaternius.com/packs/zombieapocalypsekit.html
- Original author release: https://www.patreon.com/quaternius/posts/zombie-kit-60-100385247

## License discrepancies and evidence priority

- `LICENSE.original.txt` is the mirror's actual included 374-byte CC0 license; SHA-256 `de990ef6fc68cffd7fd1ae342c4d0c823b541b8848d8f76bca5d3339f4de6f6e`.
- Its heading says “Ultimate Platformer Pack,” apparently reused boilerplate. The **specific Zombie Apocalypse Kit author's page and original author announcement**, both explicitly CC0, are the primary licensing evidence for this model.
- The independent Poly Pizza preview at https://poly.pizza/m/Hssa6NPc6W attributes this German Shepard to Quaternius and dates it March 17, 2024, consistent with the March 14 author release. Poly Pizza labels its distribution CC Attribution. No model file was downloaded from Poly Pizza, and its label is not used to establish the author's pack license.
- No paid purchase, sign-in, or access-control bypass was used. Public folder browsing worked; public author downloads were quota-blocked. The inspection copy came from a separate openly available redistribution mirror.

## Actual glTF inventory

The inventory was read from the original source glTF; the runtime adaptation may remove gear and alter geometry.

- One mesh, one skinned primitive, **4,898 triangles**, **4,077 exported vertices** (including normal/UV seams).
- Skin: `AnimalArmature`, **50 joints**, including spine/neck/head, four bones per ear, articulated front/rear legs, and a multijoint tail.
- Embedded binary geometry and embedded `Zombie_Atlas` texture; no external texture dependency.
- Eleven clips: `Attack`, `Death`, `Eating`, `HitReact_Left`, `HitReact_Right`, `Idle`, `Idle_2`, `Idle_2_HeadLow`, `Run`, `Run_Jump`, `Walk`.
- One skinned primitive is not proof of connected or watertight topology. Ear roots, skin weights, silhouette, and animation deformations are inspected in Blender during adaptation. Rendered original previews showed a friendly adventure dog, not a hostile zombie creature, but the facial shape, coat, equipment, and body proportions require substantial refinement for Khloé.

## Art-direction reference, not a model source

Bethesda's original Dogmeat/River development article:

https://bethesda.net/en-US/news/fallout-4-dogmeat-and-other-companions

It documents the real German Shepherd River as Dogmeat's reference. Use the real dog's grounded silhouette, planted ear bases, elongated muzzle, tucked waist, and companion behavior as inspiration. No Fallout/Dogmeat game meshes or textures are licensed by that article, and none were downloaded. Search results marked “model not by me” or extracted from Call of Duty/Fallout were excluded as production candidates even when uploaders selected permissive labels.

## Anatomy reference and adaptation scope

The German Shepherd Dog Club of America’s official standard informs silhouette checks: https://gsdca.org/breed-standard/ . The useful visual cues are a slightly longer-than-tall body, lean muscular torso, long wedge-shaped muzzle, non-protruding almond eyes, upright ears with grounded bases, and a low-set gently curved tail. The standard’s body length is breastbone to rear pelvis, not nose to tail.

The source is an anatomical and animation starting point, not the final Khloé design. The adaptation removes adventure gear, adjusts silhouette and face, replaces coat markings and eyes, and retains coherent skeletal deformation. No Bethesda/Fallout model, mesh, texture, or animation is included.
